cases.notes: Inbound EventSub-style webhook signature compared with a naive, non-constant-time string comparison (CWE-347) -- modeled on Twitch's real EventSub webhook receiver (docs/research/site-architecture-survey-functionality-twitch.md). The tainted value is carried in a request header, not a query/body field, so `param` is set to the literal header name `X-Signature-256` -- the same convention a query-param case uses the literal query-string key, recorded here as a deliberate judgment call (CC-LAB-0174) since this is this project's first header-carried case. `LABGEN-GO-0001` in lab/manifests/webhook_signature_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0001` (go_net_http derives the served route from cell_id, not the manifest's own `route:` field, to keep vulnerable/secure twins from colliding) -- never a PFF-* case.

url query param fetched server-side with no scheme or resolved-IP allowlist check (CWE-918) -- modeled on Twitch's real clip-thumbnail-fetch proxy (docs/research/site-architecture-survey-functionality-twitch.md). `LABGEN-GO-0003` in lab/manifests/ssrf_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0003` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001) -- never a PFF-* case.

channel_id query param used to look up per-channel analytics with no check that it matches the caller's own X-Broadcaster-Id (CWE-639/862, broken object-level authorization / IDOR) -- modeled on Twitch's real per-channel analytics API, a textbook OWASP API1:2023 BOLA surface for a public API-edge service. Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing db_row_by_id_lookup sink family and no_ownership_check/identity_match_before_fetch ops (added by CC-LAB-0063 for the corpus-examples/access-control research) -- the first lab-generator instance of this mechanism on any stack. `X-Broadcaster-Id` is a fixed demo header standing in for the caller's own identity (this stack has no session/auth system yet; the header models only the ownership-check-bypass mechanism in isolation, never a real session/auth system). `LABGEN-GO-0005` in lab/manifests/access_control_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0005` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001/0002) -- never a PFF-* case.

A Bearer JWT's own alg:none header is honored, skipping signature verification entirely and trusting the token's own forged claims (CWE-347, the real auth0/node-jsonwebtoken GHSA-8cf7-32gw-wr33 bug -- docs/research/corpus-examples/auth-session/node/vulnerable-1.js) -- modeled on a channel-owner-only settings endpoint, a realistic Bearer-JWT-protected API-edge shape for this app identity. Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing jwt_signature_verification sink family and jwt_alg_none_default/jwt_none_alg_opt_in ops (added by CC-LAB-0063 for the corpus-examples/auth-session research) -- the first lab-generator instance of this mechanism on any stack. The tainted value is carried in the Authorization header, not a query/body field, so `param` is set to the literal header name `Authorization` (the same header-carried-value convention TWCH-0001 established, CC-LAB-0174). `LABGEN-GO-0007` in lab/manifests/jwt_alg_confusion_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0007` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001/0002/0003) -- never a PFF-* case.

A session-refresh token is generated as the current nanosecond timestamp (CWE-330), trivially predictable -- an attacker who observes or roughly times one token knows every other token issued in a narrow, guessable window. Modeled on a session-token-refresh endpoint, a realistic API-edge auth shape for this app identity. Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing session_token_generation sink family and predictable_token_source/csprng_token ops (added by CC-LAB-0063 for the corpus-examples/auth-session research) -- the first lab-generator instance of this mechanism on any stack. Genuinely no tainted request input at all (unlike every other case here) -- `param`/`location` are set to the whole-body-point convention (`body`/`body`) this project already uses for other no-per-field-param whole-body cases (e.g. NFLX-0001/insecure_deserialization), even though the request body itself is unused by this mechanism; the vulnerability is entirely in the response the sink generates, not in anything the caller sends. `LABGEN-GO-0009` in lab/manifests/weak_token_entropy_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0009` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001/0002/0003/0004) -- never a PFF-* case.

A channel-profile-update endpoint unmarshals the raw request body directly onto the live channel record struct (CWE-915) -- any JSON field present, including `is_partner` (never exposed by this endpoint's own intended form), takes effect. Modeled on Twitch's real channel-profile-update surface, a realistic API-edge shape for this app identity. Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing orm_entity_bulk_assign sink family and unfiltered_object_assign/typed_schema_allowlist ops (added by CC-LAB-0063 for the corpus-examples/mass-assignment research; already instantiated on php_current/ruby_rails/php_laravel) -- the first go_net_http instance of this mechanism. `param`/`location` are set to the whole-body-point convention (`body`/`body`) this project already uses for other no-per-field-param whole-body cases (e.g. TWCH-0005/weak_token_entropy), since the privileged field (`is_partner`) is one of several JSON keys in the request body, not a single named param -- also required for `fuzzlab.harness.auto.points_from_ground_truth`'s own content-type detection, which only marks a body point as JSON when `param=="body"` exactly. `LABGEN-GO-0011` in lab/manifests/mass_assignment_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0011` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001..0005) -- never a PFF-* case.

channel_id query param used to look up a channel's subscriber roster/count with no check that it matches the caller's own X-Broadcaster-Id (CWE-639/862, broken object-level authorization / IDOR) -- modeled on Twitch's real per-channel subscriber-roster API, a second, distinct textbook OWASP API1:2023 BOLA surface alongside TWCH-0003's per-channel analytics lookup, a realistic public API-edge feature for this app identity. Reuses CC-LAB-0178's already-built read_channel_id_and_broadcaster_header source, no_ownership_check/identity_match_before_fetch transforms, and object_lookup_authorization_check sink verbatim (lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing db_row_by_id_lookup sink family) -- zero new generator code, only a new lab/manifests/access_control_subscribers_go_sample.yaml manifest and one new _ROUTE_PARAMS['/channels/subscribers'] route-profile entry in fuzzlab/labgen/emitters/go_net_http/__init__.py (config, not a new class/template), mirroring CC-LAB-0179's own zero-new-generator-code reuse-at-a-new-route precedent. `X-Broadcaster-Id` is the same fixed demo header CC-LAB-0178 already documented as modeling only the ownership-check-bypass mechanism in isolation, never a real session/auth system. `LABGEN-GO-0013` in lab/manifests/access_control_subscribers_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0013` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001..0006) -- never a PFF-* case. Verified live: AccessControlIdorStrategy (already built for TWCH-0003, keyed on vuln_class=access_control + sink shape, not per-route) confirms this new vulnerable twin with no new audit-rule/strategy code, and correctly does not confirm the secure twin (LABGEN-GO-0014).

source_url query param fetched server-side with no scheme or resolved-IP allowlist check (CWE-918) -- modeled on Twitch's real clip-import/download feature (import a clip from an externally-hosted source URL), a second, distinct real Twitch feature from TWCH-0002's clip-thumbnail-fetch proxy, not a cosmetic rename of it. Reuses CC-LAB-0172's already-built read_url_query_param source and unchecked_url_fetch/scheme_and_resolved_ip_allowlist sinks verbatim (lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing server_side_http_fetch sink family) -- zero new generator code, only a new lab/manifests/ssrf_clips_download_go_sample.yaml manifest and one new _ROUTE_PARAMS['/clips/download'] route-profile entry in fuzzlab/labgen/emitters/go_net_http/__init__.py (config, not a new class/template), mirroring CC-LAB-0183's own zero-new-generator-code reuse-at-a-new-route precedent. `LABGEN-GO-0015` in lab/manifests/ssrf_clips_download_go_sample.yaml, served at `/generated/labgen-go-0015` (same cell_id-derived-route convention as TWCH-0001..0007) -- never a PFF-* case. Verified live: SsrfInBandMarkerStrategy/SsrfOobStrategy (already built for TWCH-0002, keyed on vuln_class=ssrf + sink shape, not per-route) confirm this new vulnerable twin with no new audit-rule/strategy code, and correctly do not confirm the secure twin (LABGEN-GO-0016).
